originality.rationale: Knutsen I establishes the exact first eigenvalue but only the upper bound norm <= twice that eigenvalue (Theorem 4.1). Knutsen II, §1 and Theorem 3.1, proves a norm identity for the different left-justified canonical alphabet and specifically notes absence of this result for the middle-third alphabet. The new initial-window exponential-convolution comparison proves the all-radius norm identity, spectral simplicity and quantitative all-degree separation for the mid-third mask. A nearby Cantor–Bergman vacuum result does not imply a Gaussian STFT theorem because its Hilbert space and critical scaling differ. Searches cannot certify global novelty; specialist historical work remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The motivating author proved the explicit Gaussian eigenvalue but could bound the true operator norm only within a factor of two, and the sequel expressly left middle-third Gaussian optimality unsettled. This theorem closes that precise, motivated mathematical gap for every stage and positive radius, gives spectral simplicity and a strict explicit all-mode gap, and isolates an independently useful sliding-window criterion. The exact operator norm is needed for sharp fractal Gaussian concentration estimates; it is not merely a restatement of the known product.
